challenges.name: api-autoscaler
challenges.title: Autoscale the api for the lunch and dinner peaks
challenges.description: Rice Rocket's api needs 3 pods at night and up to 3 times more at 11:00 and 18:00. The first autoscaler showed `<unknown>/70%` and never scaled, a release applied during the peak cut 9 pods back to 3, and after the peak the pod count went up and down every minute. The editor holds `k8s/api.yaml` (the api Deployment and its HorizontalPodAutoscaler) with key blocks missing, each marked by a `# [ ]` line; some pieces are wrong on purpose. Fill every line so that: each api pod reserves 250m CPU and 256Mi memory (512Mi memory limit); the HPA resizes the api Deployment between 3 and 12 pods, aiming at 70% of the reserved CPU; it may double the pods each minute but removes pods only after 5 calm minutes; and applying the file during a peak never changes the pod count. Run grades the file with a simulator of the autoscaler's documented algorithm on a recorded day of load.
hints: Walk through the three incidents: what does the autoscaler divide the CPU use by, which field of the Deployment does `kubectl apply` write back, and what makes the autoscaler wait before it removes pods?

Look at `resources.requests` of the container, `spec.replicas` of the Deployment (and what happens when it is absent), and in the HPA: `scaleTargetRef`, `minReplicas` / `maxReplicas`, `metrics[].resource.target` (`type: Utilization` with `averageUtilization`), and `behavior.scaleUp` / `behavior.scaleDown`.

A worker that should stay between 2 and 8 pods at 60% of a 500m request, grow by at most 4 pods a minute and shrink after 10 calm minutes: `resources: { requests: { cpu: 500m } }` on its container, no `replicas:` in its Deployment, and an HPA with `minReplicas: 2`, `maxReplicas: 8`, `metrics: [{ type: Resource, resource: { name: cpu, target: { type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 60 } } }]`, `behavior: { scaleUp: { policies: [{ type: Pods, value: 4, periodSeconds: 60 }] }, scaleDown: { stabilizationWindowSeconds: 600 } }`.

tests.name: The HPA scales the api Deployment on 70% of a 250m CPU request
A lunch peak: 3 pods at night, up to 11 at the peak, back to 3 five calm minutes later
A release applied in the middle of the peak does not cut the pod count
Load that swings every minute keeps 6 pods steady instead of flapping
Night load stays at 3 pods and a load spike stops at 12
